chunks: 3651 - And it is narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar al-Qalanisi, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “We make caps and place old cotton inside them, then we sell them and do not make clear to them what is inside them.” So he said: “Indeed, I certainly prefer for you that you make clear to them what is inside them.”

key_terms.الْقَلَانِسَ: caps or head-coverings being manufactured and sold
key_terms.الْقُطْنَ الْعَتِيقَ: old cotton used as filling inside the caps
key_terms.تُبَيِّنَ: that you clearly inform or disclose
key_terms.وَلَا نُبَيِّنُ: we do not clarify or disclose

ai.seo_question: Should a seller disclose hidden defects or lower-quality materials in merchandise?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches transparency and honesty in trade. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام expresses approval for informing buyers about the actual contents of the goods being sold, indicating an ethical standard in commercial dealings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3651 - Al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar al-Qalanisi narrated:

I said to Abu Abdullah (as), 'We make caps and place old cotton inside them, then sell them without informing the buyers of what is inside.'
Imam (as) replied: 'I would prefer that you inform them about what is inside.'
